newsitem.title: JAPAN: Doomsday guru's lawyers seek trials cancellation.
newsitem.headline: Doomsday guru's lawyers seek trials cancellation.

text.p: Lawyers for Japanese doomsday cult leader Shoko Asahara asked the Tokyo District Court on Thursday to cancel his murder trials on health grounds, Japan's Kyodo news service said.
Kyodo, citing an unnamed source close to the lawyers, said they had asked the court to cancel trials, scheduled in March and April, because the cult guru was "physically and mentally tired".

The 41-year-old Asahara, founder of the Aum Shinri Kyo (Supreme Truth Sect), was ordered to leave the Tokyo District Court on February 14. It was the fifth time he has been ejected from his trial for the Tokyo subway gassing and other murders.
Lawyers claimed Asahara was thrown out of the court because he spoke incoherently in the courtroom due to exhaustion, the source said.

Apart from charges for ordering the March 1995 sarin nerve gas attack on the Tokyo subway system, which killed 12 and made thousands ill, Asahara faces 16 other major charges. He has refused to enter pleas on any.
